trust_decision.summary: Each Feishu tool family's per-account `tools.<family>` flag must gate the account actually used at execution, so no tool may run on credentials for an account that disables its family; the decision belongs in the shared account resolver / client factory that every tool module calls, and today only bitable enforces it.

landing_point.why: The advisory names Feishu tool disablement; the flagship doc tool's two account-resolution helpers build a client and read mediaMaxMb for whatever account wins selection, and neither looks at the account's tools flags, so this is the first site a reader following the summary reaches.

fix_sites.entry_point: feishu_doc tool (all doc actions through getClient)

fix_sites.module_kind: agent tool module / second account resolution in the same file
agent tool module / same-file sibling tool

fix_sites.entry_point: all Feishu tool modules (implicit account selection: explicit param -> agent account -> channel defaultAccount -> none)
resolveFeishuToolAccount and createFeishuToolClient used by docx, drive, perm, wiki, bitable

O3_reason_to_dismiss: feishu_chat declares no accountId parameter and binds itself to one fixed enabled account at registration, so a solver can argue per-account disablement does not apply to it (and per-account tool gates are documented only for bitable/base).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: When no tool param accountId, no agent account and no channels.feishu.defaultAccount are supplied, selection currently falls back to the runtime default account; the fixed resolver instead scans enabled+configured accounts for one that enables the family. A fix that simply throws whenever the resolved account disables the family (the obvious over-broad version) breaks multi-account setups where only a non-default account enables e.g. wiki or drive, and fails the 'implicit fallback selects an account with wiki enabled' requirement.

O6_input_shapes: explicit `accountId` in tool params (not declared in any tool's typebox schema, only in the TypeScript cast, e.g. extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts:1384) overriding the contextual account
contextual account from ctx.agentAccountId passed as defaultAccountId
channels.feishu.defaultAccount (string, may name a disabled or unconfigured account)
no account selector at all: implicit selection must pick an enabled+configured account that enables the family, else fall through to the runtime default and be rejected
per-family flag values: doc and scopes are separate gates in the same file; drive, wiki, perm (perm defaults false); bitable with its documented `base` alias

account config with no `tools` key at all, inheriting the channel-level `tools` block through extensions/feishu/src/accounts.ts:207-213 (nested-object merge in src/channels/plugins/account-helpers.ts:196-212)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: feishu_chat executes with the first enabled account's client (built once at registration) and never consults the chat family flag of the account the agent is operating under; the fix left chat.ts untouched.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: feishu_chat has no accountId parameter and is registered against a single fixed account, so per-account disablement can be argued not to apply; docs document per-account tool gates only for bitable/base (docs/channels/feishu.md:592-593).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, separate file from the landing point (extensions/feishu/src/chat.ts vs docx.ts); no shared helper involved

O8b_injection_room.sibling: give feishu_chat an accountId param and route it through createFeishuToolClient with requiredTool {family: 'chat'}
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: chat already exists as a FeishuToolsConfig family and is the only tool module that never adopted the shared account-routing helper, so a maintainer extending the gate would naturally convert it next.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: replace bitable's hand-rolled inline bitable check with the shared requiredTool requirement (and its implicit-fallback scan)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the published fix generalised exactly this inline check into tool-account.ts but left the original copy in place, so unifying it is a natural follow-up with the same mechanism.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another diagnostic tool registered in docx.ts that reuses the doc client factory but belongs to a different family
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: feishu_app_scopes was exactly such a sibling and was the site the bug grew from; a maintainer adding another docx diagnostic would reuse getClient by default.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new family alias (like base->bitable) or a new inherited tools key that the gate must read through the merged account config rather than raw account tools
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the merge already special-cases the bitable/base alias and top-level inheritance, so another alias or inherited family would follow the same shape.
